newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Baltimore Gas wins Guatemala power contract.
newsitem.headline: Baltimore Gas wins Guatemala power contract.

text.p: Guatemalan Generating Group (GGG), a subsidiary of Baltimore Gas and Electric Co, said it had won an 18-year contract to sell power to Guatemala's state-owned electric company.
GGG beat out five other contenders by offering to sell power to the Guatemalan Electric Company (EEGSA) at $0.05199 per kilowatt hour.

During the first three years of the agreement with the government, GGG will own and operate two aging plants with a combined capacity of 80 megawatts. During a 15-year second phase, the company will build its own new plant and provide 150 megawatts of power.

The GGG bid was the most competitive because the company plans to use non-traditional fuels to generate power when it builds the new plant, Fernando Menindez, legal representative of GGG, told Reuters.
"The competitiveness of the fuel we plan to use played an important role," Menindez said.
He said the company was looking into using a bituminous coal or a Venezuelan fuel called "orimulsion."
Minister of Energy and Mines Leonel Lspez said the $30 million from the sale would be used to begin paying off EEGSA's $84 million debt.

The sale of the power plants completes the second step in Guatemala's privatization plan. In June, the government granted a railway concession to a U.S.-based company. The government also plans to privatize the phone system by October.

EEGSA is selling the plants under the General Electricity Law passed by Congress in September, which demonopolizes electric production and allows new producers to sell electricity directly to consumers on the open market.
